summary: Project ForgetMeNot is an interactive digital storybook and archive of the abandoned artifacts from retired missions. Designed specifically for school-aged children and young space enthusiasts, the experience bridges the gap between dense technical mission logs and emotional storytelling—giving a voice to the silent machines that pushed the boundaries of human exploration. It is an engaging and personal narrative that is bound to draw users towards learning more about space history and science.
details:
Project Overview:

Across the silent plains of the Moon and the red dust of Mars sit dozens of retired spacecraft—machines that once carried humanity's boldest questions across the solar system before falling quiet. Project ForgetMeNot transforms these discarded robotic pioneers into living storytellers, inviting school-aged children to step inside the personal histories of NASA’s off-world explorers.

Rather than treating space history as a list of mission dates, coordinates, and technical specs, the platform reframes engineering as an act of human perseverance and heart. Beginning with an intimate look at NASA’s Ingenuity ("Ginny") helicopter and expanding into an interactive archive of historic lunar and Martian hardware, the experience blends narrative immersion with verified NASA mission science. Every chapter is crafted to spark curiosity in young minds, turning passive readers into active explorers ready to carry humanity's story among the stars forward.

Narrative Structure:

The experience begins from a third-person perspective inside a cozy, atmospheric room, where the user receives a mysterious piece of mail. Opening the envelope reveals an exciting invitation that draws the young explorer out of their everyday world and into an interactive journey through off-world space history.

From there, the story transports the user to Mars to witness the firsthand journey of NASA’s Ingenuity ("Ginny") helicopter—experiencing the grit, challenges, and triumph of achieving powered flight on another planet. At the close of its tale, Ingenuity leaves behind a personal, heartfelt letter asking simply to be remembered and passing the torch of curiosity to the reader.

This heartfelt request unlocks The Abandoned Archive, an interactive digital flipbook filled with categorized chapters on other legendary equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars—including the Lunar Roving Vehicles, Viking, Pathfinder, Curiosity, and InSight. Finally, the journey concludes with The Explorer's Challenge, a gamified trivia quiz where students test their knowledge of these historic machines and solidify what they discovered along the way.

Tech Stack:

Frontend: HTML5, CSS (Tailwind v4), TypeScript / React 19
Hosting & Architecture: Client-side interactive web application built on TanStack Start and Vite, designed as a full-screen, step-by-step narrative player.
Interactive Visualization: Custom 360° celestial sphere rendered with HTML5 Canvas 2D, featuring cursor-driven panoramic navigation, dynamic starfields, and realistic Earth texture mapping.
